heading_path: Access entire config object from plugins
hits.tldr: Tailwind plugins can now access the entire config object by calling config() with no arguments.
Use @source not directive to exclude specific paths from Tailwind class scanning.
Dynamic group-* and peer-* variants allow custom selectors to be passed in square brackets for on-the-fly variant creation.
Tailwind resets border styles on all elements so the `border` class adds a solid 1px border using currentColor.

content.text:
These docs don't have a guide for writing third-party plugins. v3's "Plugins" page has no v4 counterpart in this folder, though the index search only surfaced the `@plugin` directive.

Plugins are still supported. `@plugin` loads a "legacy JavaScript-based plugin" from a package name or local path (e.g. `@plugin "@tailwindcss/typography";`). It can be combined with `@theme`, `@utility` and other CSS-driven features (`src/docs/functions-and-directives.mdx`, "Compatibility", lines 276–322).

The docs call it "legacy" and give no authoring API, so I can't say from them whether JS plugins are meant for the long term. They do point to CSS-first features (`@utility`, `@theme`) for new customization.
